tagline.text: A hidden lagoon behind a cave door that opens only at low tide

location.label: Location
location.text: Socorro, Bucas Grande Island, Surigao del Norte

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: March–July (calm seas, when jellyfish are plentiful)

image.credit: Michael Angelo Luna / CC BY-SA 4.0 / Wikimedia Commons

children.text: A hidden lagoon on Bucas Grande Island southwest of Siargao. Passing through a cave entrance accessible only at low tide reveals a mysterious lake ringed by limestone islands. With stingless jellyfish, a swimmable lake, a glowing sea cave, and cliff jumping, it's one of Siargao's best day-trip adventures.

Sohoton Cove is a lagoon area on Bucas Grande Island, off Siargao's southwest coast, administratively part of Socorro Municipality in Surigao del Norte. Around Bucas Grande, dozens of small limestone islands rise from the sea like mushrooms, so the scenery resembles famous limestone coastlines in Southeast Asia from the moment your bangka enters. This area, too, is managed as part of the Siargao Island Protected Landscape and Seascape.

The key to Sohoton Cove is its entrance. The only way into the lagoon is through a single low cave beneath a rock cliff, and this cave is only exposed above water — enough for a small boat to pass — at low tide. When the tide comes in, the entrance is fully submerged, sealing inside from outside, so locals have long regarded this place as a hidden refuge. Passing through the cave reveals a quiet turquoise lake surrounded by jungle-covered limestone walls, and that moment of awe is the highlight of a Sohoton trip.

Inside and around the lagoon are Hagukan Cave, which glows blue when you swim inside; Makukuob Cave, where you dive in and swim under a rock to exit the other side; and, depending on the season, a jellyfish lake where thousands of stingless jellyfish drift. To protect the area, motorized bangkas are restricted inside the lagoon, so you get around by small oar-powered boats or kayaks piloted by local guides.
Most visitors come on a day tour departing from General Luna, Siargao. The round-trip bangka ride alone takes
4–5 hours

, making for a long day, but the chance to experience the cave, the lagoon, the jellyfish lake, and cliff jumping all in one trip keeps it consistently popular among Siargao travelers. It suits confident swimmers and adventure-minded travelers especially well.

blocks.title: Passing through the low-tide cave entrance

children.text: You sit low in a small boat steered by your guide and pass through the narrow cave entrance into the lagoon. The moment you emerge from the dim cave into a sunlit lake stays with you for a long time.

blocks.title: Kayaking and rowing around the lagoon

children.text: Inside the lagoon, you slowly tour the limestone islands by rowboat or kayak. The water is so clear that in shallow spots, coral and fish are visible right through the surface.

The jellyfish lake on Bucas Grande is home to jellyfish with almost no sting, so you can wear a snorkel mask and swim among them. Their numbers vary greatly with season and water temperature, typically peaking from March to
July

Swimming through a small gap in the seaward cliff, the interior glows blue with sunlight reflecting off the water. The entrance is low, so you need to duck your head, and you should always go in with a guide and a life vest.

blocks.title: Jumping and diving through Makukuob Cave

children.text: A test-of-nerve course where you jump into the water from a high rock inside the cave, then briefly dive beneath the rock to exit into the open sea outside. If you're not up for it, just watching is plenty of fun too.
Around the lagoon are several jump platforms of different heights, letting you leap into the sea from
up. Only jump from spots where your guide has confirmed the depth.

blocks.title: Bangka cruise among the limestone islands

children.text: On the way to and from Sohoton, you pass mushroom-shaped limestone islands and clear shallow water. The water color is most beautiful when the afternoon sun hits it.

items.title: By boat
items.subtitle: Visiting Surigao City or Socorro directly

children.text: A passenger bangka runs from Surigao City to Socorro village on Bucas Grande, taking about
2–3 hours

. Boats run only once or twice a day, so check with the Surigao port ticket office. Once in Socorro, you register at the tourism office and are assigned a local guide and bangka to reach the lagoon. Staying overnight on Bucas Grande has the advantage of touring at less crowded times.

Inside the lagoon, you can only move by small oar-powered boats or kayaks paddled by local residents, to prevent motor noise and pollution. This is usually included in the tour fee, but some operators charge separately for the small boat, so confirm when booking.
Because Sohoton Cove requires a long sea crossing,
March
through
July
, when the seas are calm, is the best time. Skies are clear during this period, making the lagoon's water color vivid, and this is also when the jellyfish lake tends to have the most jellyfish.
August
through
October
is generally still travelable, but some days are affected by southwest winds and swells.
From
November
to
February

, the northeast monsoon brings frequent rain and rough seas, which can cancel tours or make the crossing very difficult. Jellyfish numbers vary greatly year to year, and in some years there are almost none in a given month, so it's best to keep expectations flexible. Above all, passing through the cave entrance depends on low tide, so tour operators set the departure time according to a tide table.

Most travelers stay in General Luna, Siargao, and visit as a day trip. General Luna has a wide range of lodging from hostels to boutique resorts, at about
per night. For a more secluded experience, you can stay at a small resort in Socorro village on Bucas Grande or between the limestone islands (about
per night), though options are few and amenities basic, so book ahead.

Tour lunch is usually served at an island hut or floating restaurant, typically a generous spread of grilled fish and squid, shrimp, fruit like mango and watermelon, and rice. Around Socorro village, crab and shellfish dishes are well known. There are almost no shops along the tour route, so it's best to bring snacks and water from General Luna before departing.
When booking, check item by item whether the environmental fee, entrance fee, and inner boat cost are included in the tour price, and prepare cash for any extras.
The round-trip bangka ride is long and can be rough, so if you're prone to motion sickness, take medication
30 minutes
before departure.
You'll get wet in the caves and at the jump platforms, so a waterproof bag, a waterproof phone case, and aqua shoes are essential.
In the jellyfish lake, swim slowly so you don't grab jellyfish with your hands or kick them with fins, and skip sunscreen if possible, or use only reef-safe products.
If you're not a confident swimmer, wear a life vest, and it's fine to just watch Hagukan and Makukuob caves from outside.
There's little shade on the bangka, so bring a long-sleeve rash guard, a hat, and sunglasses.
Photos inside the lagoon come out most vivid between
10 AM and 1 PM
, when the sunlight is high.
The cave entrance floods at high tide. You must exit the lagoon within the time your guide sets, and swimming toward the cave alone is very dangerous.
Only dive and jump in Hagukan and Makukuob caves under the direction of a local guide who knows the depths and rock positions.
The lagoon and jellyfish lake are protected areas, so collecting coral or jellyfish, littering, and motor use are prohibited.
Entrance fees, visitor limits, and whether the jellyfish lake is open can change by decision of the Socorro local government, so check the latest notices.
Tours can be canceled during the northeast monsoon season and when typhoons are forecast; it's safer to decline any pressure to depart anyway.
Cell signal is absent for long stretches, making emergency contact difficult. Leave your itinerary and contact details with the tour operator and your accommodation.
